# Data processing

Data processing gives a claim producer versioned staging. A node writes into a candidate rather than into the live data, and the candidate becomes a version only when the node succeeds.

This is a mix-in on a claim producer, not a standalone service. Serve `DataProcessing` from the same process as your `ClaimProducer`, and advertise `data_processing` in your `ClaimProducer.Capabilities` `protocols` list. Rimsky checks that a producer advertising the protocol actually serves it and refuses to start when it does not. An operator also names the protocol in the deployment's `claim_producers.<name>.protocols`, or declares the peer under `data_processors` instead.

Read the [claim producer guide](claim-producer.md) first.

Proto file: `data_processing.proto`.

## The RPCs

| RPC | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `Capabilities(google.protobuf.Empty) → DataProcessingCapabilities` | Advertise what you can stage |
| `BeginCandidate(BeginCandidateRequest) → BeginCandidateResponse` | Open a candidate for a claim |
| `CommitCandidate(CommitCandidateRequest) → CommitCandidateResponse` | Promote a candidate to a version |
| `AbandonCandidate(AbandonCandidateRequest) → google.protobuf.Empty` | Drop a candidate |
| `ListVersions(ListVersionsRequest) → ListVersionsResponse` | List a claim's committed versions |
| `ListPartitions(ListPartitionsRequest) → ListPartitionsResponse` | List a version's partitions |
| `GetVersionSchema(GetVersionSchemaRequest) → GetVersionSchemaResponse` | Return a version's schema |

## Advertising yourself

`DataProcessingCapabilities` carries four string lists:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `data_shapes` | The shapes of data you can hold. Must be non-empty. |
| `materializations` | The materializations you can write. Must be non-empty. |
| `partition_kinds` | The partitioning schemes you support |
| `aggregators` | The aggregations you can apply |

The conformance run drives one begin-and-commit cycle per advertised materialization, so advertise only what you can actually write.

## The candidate lifecycle

Rimsky opens a candidate when it acquires a sub-claim, and it closes that candidate when the node settles.

`BeginCandidate` takes `claim_handle_id`, an opaque `sub_scope_descriptor`, and an `idempotency_key`. It returns a `candidate_handle` — opaque bytes that identify this candidate for the rest of its life. Rimsky carries the handle into the node's dispatch as `ClaimProducerHandle.candidate_handle`, so the executor can write into the candidate.

`CommitCandidate` takes the handle and returns `candidate_metadata`. It promotes the candidate to a version.

`AbandonCandidate` takes the handle and drops the candidate.

Four rules the conformance run enforces:

- **`BeginCandidate` is idempotent on its key.** Two calls with the same `claim_handle_id` and `idempotency_key` must return byte-equal `candidate_handle` values.
- **An abandoned candidate leaves no version.** After `AbandonCandidate`, `ListVersions` for that claim must return nothing the candidate wrote.
- **An abandoned candidate rejects a later commit.** `CommitCandidate` on an already-abandoned handle must fail. Collect the candidate and refuse.
- **An unknown handle fails.** `AbandonCandidate` on bytes you never issued must return an error rather than succeeding quietly.

Rimsky calls `AbandonCandidate` when acquisition fails partway, and `CommitCandidate` or `AbandonCandidate` when the node settles.

## Reading versions back

`ListVersions` takes a `claim_handle_id` and returns `VersionMetadata` rows, each with `version_id`, `committed_at`, and `producer_metadata`. Give every version a non-empty `version_id`, and give each one a distinct id even under concurrent commits.

`ListPartitions` takes `claim_handle_id` and `version_id` and returns `PartitionDescriptor` rows, each with `partition_key` and `partition_metadata`.

`GetVersionSchema` takes `claim_handle_id` and `version_id` and returns the version's `schema` as bytes.

## Concurrency

The conformance run opens eight candidates on one `claim_handle_id` at once, commits them all, and requires exactly eight versions with eight distinct ids. Two writers staging into the same claim must not collide, and neither may lose a commit.

## Proving it

```
rimsky conformance data-processing --endpoint grpc://localhost:9101
```

The suite requires gRPC. There is no HTTP+JSON bridge for `DataProcessing`.
